title: Attribute the 14% Quake spends not running — the biggest bucket is the one the current instrument is structurally blind to
layer: measurement (LD_PRELOAD sleep accounting in the client + a matching counter in xshim), aimed at the lvdesk↔client and paging boundaries
mechanism: docs/smp-finish-plan.md fixes the goal arithmetic: "The ceiling is removing Quake's waits: 17.3 / 0.84 = 20.6 fps. The 20 fps goal is the 16% Quake spends not running." The only instrument ever pointed at those waits is rootfs/waitsamp, a /proc sampler, and its own recorded run (artifacts/quake/wait-063645/out.txt, 969 frames / 64.5 s / 15.0 fps, 1,111 samples) reports: 86.0% R running, 7.3% S with sys=0 pc=0, 2.6% D with sys=0 pc=0, 1.8% S in syscall 414 (ppoll_time64), and ~1.6% D scattered over faulting PCs. The 7.3% is the LARGEST non-running bucket and it is exactly the bucket the tool admits it cannot read — the plan's own note says "Short sleeps (under a few ms, which read 'running' by the time /proc/<tid>/syscall is read) make ~10%". The conclusion drawn from that run, "No single wait is worth chasing", is therefore unsupported for 4.9 ms of a 66.6 ms frame. A few-hundred-Hz sampler is the wrong instrument for a 1-5 ms event happening 15 times a second; counting is. Build the counting instrument: an LD_PRELOAD shim (measurement only — the pattern already used by rootfs/syscount.c in frame-path-plan step 1 and rootfs/ioctlprof.c) interposing every syscall that can sleep — ppoll, poll, pselect, futex, nanosleep, clock_nanosleep, read, write, recvmsg, sendmsg, ioctl — timing each with the rdtime CSR rather than clock_gettime (lvdesk/lvdesk.c fsg_rdtime exists precisely because clock_gettime cost more than the thing it measured: 16.4% of lvdesk's on-CPU samples were in libc's clock_gettime page), keyed by return address, dumped on SIGUSR2 as count + total + histogram. Second half, and it is what makes the answer trustworthy: a counter in xshim of the wall time from a client's doorbell arriving to its reply leaving, so the same interval is measured from both ends and the two have to agree. Note the rv32 varargs trap — ioctlprof's dump prints garbage; use plain %lu.
evidence: artifacts/quake/wait-063645/out.txt — WS 86.0% R; 7.3% (81 samples) S sys=0 pc=0; 2.6% (29) D sys=0 pc=0; 1.8% (20) S sys=414 pc in libc (ppoll); RESULT 969 frames 64.5 s 15.0 fps

docs/smp-finish-plan.md, "Quake, where CPU0 goes and what it waits on (2026-09-22)" — running 86%, short sleeps ~10%, page faults ~2%, ppoll 1.8%, "No single wait is worth chasing"; and "The ceiling is removing Quake's waits: 17.3 / 0.84 = 20.6 fps"

rootfs/waitsamp.c (the sampler being repaired); rootfs/syscount.c and docs/frame-path-plan.md section 1 (LD_PRELOAD interposer precedent: 2.2 socket syscalls/frame, one write 3.1 ms, one recvmsg 13.9 ms)
lvdesk/lvdesk.c ~4295-4400 — fsg_rdtime/fsg_clock_init: rdtime probed under SIGILL, calibrated once, because four clock_gettime calls a frame were 16.4% of lvdesk's samples

artifacts/quake/h1s-062518/pcs.txt — 12,000 CPU0 PC samples: kernel 4,832, program 5,950, libs 934, M-mode 61. The PC sampler cannot see a sleeping thread at all, which is why it never produced this number
magnitude_estimate: Buys 0 fps by itself; it bounds everything else. 7.3% of wall is 4.9 ms of a 66.6 ms frame, and the total non-running 14% is the entire stated distance from 17.3 fps to the 20.6 fps ceiling. Cost is one board session: no kernel build, no reflash, no partition change.
rule_check: Measurement-only LD_PRELOAD into the game — the established practice here (syscount was preloaded into prboom for a timedemo). The app binary is not rebuilt, relinked, reconfigured or wrapped for speed, and nothing is installed on its path. No feature disabled, no upstream code patched, no RAM cost beyond the shim, apps stay on SD.
prior_attempts: waitsamp (2026-09-22) is the existing attempt and is what this repairs. syscount (2026-09-10) counted syscalls per frame but not their durations, and its threshold question (">= 3 socket syscalls per frame") was about overhead, not about blocked time. ioctlprof times ioctls only. Deliberately distinct from the already-proposed "symbolise the user side of the profile" and "profile the whole run tagged by phase": both sample the PC while the thread is ON a CPU and are structurally blind to sleeping, which is the entire 14% in question.

title: Take the compositor off the game's per-frame critical path: double-buffer the MIT-SHM surface inside our libSDL, and make xshim send ShmCompletion
layer: shared libraries the app loads (SDL 1.2 X11 video driver) + xshim's MIT-SHM implementation
mechanism: Every SDL 1.2 frame ends in X11_NormalUpdate: XShmPutImage with send_event=False, then XSync. The client therefore blocks until the server has copied its segment out. Late present already moved the *present* out of that window — xshim.c:9615-9617 does out_flush(c) and only then late_present_drain(), "replies are on the wire: now paint" — and that was worth +13% on Doom (34.6 → 39.1 fps). What is still inside the window is the copy itself (76,800 bytes for Quake at 320x240x8) plus two process wakes, one of which is cross-hart at the measured ~165 us. docs/frame-path-plan.md closed this line with "the XSync semantics require the wait". That is true of XSync and false of MIT-SHM: the extension carries a ShmCompletion event precisely so a client can carry on and learn later when the server is done. Our server never sends one — it advertises MIT-SHM with event base 0, commented "no events: we never ShmCompletion, and nothing asks us to" (xshim.c:6186-6192) — and our SDL never asks. Both ends are ours. Two routes: (a) send_event=True plus ShmCompletion, with SDL's wait moved from the end of the flip to the next SDL_Flip/UpdateRects/LockSurface, which for TyrQuake puts the game logic of Host_Frame (input, client move, server frame) between the flip and the wait; (b) two segments alternated, with the app-visible address held constant by mmap(MAP_FIXED) of the other segment over it after each flip — this matters because TyrQuake caches vid.buffer = surface->pixels once at SetVideoMode, which is what makes a naive buffer swap unsafe, and it removes the wait entirely rather than moving it, at the cost of one extra buffer and one mmap per frame. Crucially neither route adopts the client's segment: the server still copies, so the failure that killed server-side adoption (xshim.c:5404-5424, "Adopting left prboom rendering its next frame into the pixels we had not drawn yet" — the weapon sprite flicker no instrument here could see) cannot recur.
evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:6186-6192 — MIT-SHM advertised with d24[2] = 0, "no events: we never ShmCompletion, and nothing asks us to"; the sendEvent byte at r+28 is parsed in the comment and never read
lvdesk/xshim.c:5404-5424 — "COPY. Always. Do not adopt the client's segment" and why adoption was worth ~11% and is still illegal
lvdesk/xshim.c:9615-9617 — out_flush then late_present_drain; docs/worklog-2026-09-21-latepresent — late present +13%, gaps <25 ms 1219 → 2626

docs/frame-path-plan.md sections 1 and 4 — 2.2 socket syscalls/frame, write 3.1 ms, recvmsg 13.9 ms, "the XSync semantics require the wait", step 4 DEAD; both measured on ONE core, before SMP and before XLITE-RING
artifacts/quake/wait-063645/out.txt — 1.8% of wall in ppoll (the ring wait for lvdesk's reply) plus 7.3% unattributed short sleeps; docs/smp-finish-plan.md — cross-hart wake ~165 us, ceiling 20.6 fps
buildroot/package/sdl/sdl.mk (SDL 1.2.15, four patches already carried) and buildroot-external/patches/bluez5_utils/0001-*.patch (where our own package patches live)
magnitude_estimate: Floor: the measured ppoll share alone, 1.8% of wall ≈ +1.8% fps (16.6 → 16.9). Ceiling: the whole non-running 14%, i.e. the stated 20.6 fps, if proposal 1 finds the 7.3% of short sleeps is this wait. Route (b) additionally removes one cross-hart wake pair per frame (~0.33 ms of 66.6 ms, 0.5%). Honest spread +2% to +8%; proposal 1 decides where in that range before anything is built. RAM cost 77 KB (8bpp 320x240) or 154 KB (16bpp) of anonymous shared memory.
rule_check: The game binary is untouched: no rebuild, no relink, no build define, no config steering, no wrapper — SDL 1.2 is one of the shared libraries the rules explicitly place on the platform side, and it is not on the do-not-patch list (Xorg, mesa, dwc2 core). Apps stay on SD; the extra buffer is not XIP. Nothing is disabled. Memory cost is 0.5-1% of the 15.4 MB and is stated, not hidden.
prior_attempts: frame-path-plan step 4 (shared-memory X transport) was killed on "the two syscalls a frame are the server's work" — measured single-core, pre-ring, and it argued the wait was unavoidable rather than movable. Server-side adoption of the segment was built, measured 31.7 vs 29.4 fps, and rejected as illegal and visibly broken. MIT-SHM 1.2 (ShmAttachFd/ShmCreateSegment) is implemented and measured inside the band (31.6 fps) — but SDL 1.2 only ever calls XShmAttach, which is why that work never touched this path. A client-side copy in xlite was rejected on arithmetic (0.45-0.75 ms on CPU0 per 77 KB); route (b) adds no copy. Late present (2026-09-21, +13%) is the adjacent half of the same idea and this is the half it did not do. Not in the round-3 list, which contains no SDL flip/XSync item (only "deadline driven sdl 1 2 timer").

title: Give the MIT-SHM row hash the stand-down its two siblings already have — it is the only one that runs, and it runs inside the client's blocked window
layer: xshim (lvdesk/xshim.c, mitshm_request ShmPutImage)
mechanism: This tree contains three row-change scanners and the wrong one is enabled. The xlite-SHM scanner (xshim.c:617-680, xlrd_on) is OFF by default with the reason written in the file: "Measured, prboom playing demo1: 0% of rows unchanged ... Untested code in a hot path is a liability". lvdesk's fullscreen scanner (lvdesk.c:4536-4560, fsrh) is OFF by default because it "kept 59 rows out of 2,031,184", and it carries an adaptive stand-down — scan, and if fewer than an eighth of rows are unchanged, skip scanning for 63 frames (fsrh_probe). The MIT-SHM scanner — the only path prboom, TyrQuake and every stock SDL 1.2 client actually takes — is ON by default (rowdmg_on) with no stand-down at all: it hashes every byte of every frame in a scalar word loop, on the one request the client is blocked waiting for. The in-file justification is that the hash is free because those bytes are read to copy them anyway. The file's own measurement contradicts it: narrowing the hash from 64-bit to 32-bit FNV moved windowed Doom from 29.7 to 30.5 fps (xshim.c:5455-5462). If the ALU were free, halving its cost could not have bought 2.7% of a frame. For a client that keeps zero rows, the whole of that cost is loss, and it is charged to the client's critical path rather than to CPU1's spare capacity. Fix: move the stand-down that is already written twice in this tree onto the path that runs — hash, and when a scan keeps under an eighth of the rows, copy without hashing for the next 63 frames and report the whole rectangle. For these clients the fallback costs nothing downstream, because they are already damaging every row.
evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:617-628 — rowdmg_on(): default ON, XSHIM_NOROWDMG=1 already exists as a runtime toggle
lvdesk/xshim.c:5437-5520 — the fused hash-and-copy loop, run unconditionally per row per ShmPutImage, with no probe or stand-down
lvdesk/xshim.c:5455-5462 — "It cost more than it saved: 29.7 fps against 30.5" (64-bit vs 32-bit FNV), the datum that prices the hash
lvdesk/xshim.c:657-676 — xlrd: "prboom playing demo1: 0% of rows unchanged", off by default
lvdesk/lvdesk.c:4536-4560 and the fsrh_begin/fsrh_probe stand-down — "59 rows kept out of 2,031,184, and the adaptive probe stood the scan down on 9,691 of 10,008 presents", off by default
lvdesk/xshim.c:9615-9617 — the reply is flushed at the end of client_data, so the hash-copy is inside the interval the client blocks on
magnitude_estimate: Roughly two ALU ops per 4 bytes over 76,800 bytes a frame; the FNV-width datum prices the whole hash at the order of 2-3% of a frame, and it lands on Quake's blocked path rather than on CPU1. Expect +1% to +3% (16.6 → 16.8-17.1 fps). Small — but the first arm costs nothing to run: XSHIM_NOROWDMG=1 in /etc/lvdesk.env (with `export`, the trap that made late present read as neutral) and a warm-board A/B answers it in one session, with a still client checked in the same session to decide stand-down versus removal.
rule_check: Our own server code. No app rebuild, relink or config. No feature disabled. No upstream code patched. RAM goes down slightly (the per-window rowhash array is freed while stood down). Apps stay on SD.
prior_attempts: The 64→32-bit FNV narrowing was measured and shipped (+2.7%). The stand-down design was written twice — xlrd in xshim and fsrh in lvdesk — and both were defaulted off after measuring an action game keeps no rows. Nobody carried that conclusion back to the MIT-SHM path, which is the one that runs. Distinct from the proposed "the fullscreen present hashes the same ...": fsrh, the fullscreen hash, is off by default and costs nothing today; this is the xshim-side hash that is on. If that proposal turns out to cover this same asymmetry, treat this entry as its measurement plan — the free XSHIM_NOROWDMG arm has not been run on Quake.

title: Slow the memory down on purpose: a PSRAM/flash clock differential that prices every cache idea at once
layer: firmware-hart0
mechanism: Nobody on this board has ever measured what fraction of wall clock is spent waiting on memory. Every memory number here is a ratio from a microbenchmark ("XIP is ~6x RAM", "102 MB/s copy", "chase 274-316 ns"), never a share of a real workload. The two memory controllers are independent (CONFIG_SOC_MEMSPI_IS_INDEPENDENT, CONFIG_SOC_PSRAM_MEMSPI_IS_INDEPENDENT) and both have slower settings already offered by Kconfig: PSRAM is octal at 250 MHz with 200/100/40 available, flash is QIO 80M with 40M/20M available. Build loaders at (flash 80, PSRAM 250) = today, (80, 100), (40, 250) and run the identical Quake timedemo, Doom, CoreMark, pingpong and membw at each point. Halving a memory clock roughly doubles that memory's service time, so the slope of run time against 1/clock IS the fraction of run time spent waiting on it, measured separately for instruction fetch (flash: kernel XIP text, and the XIP userspace closure - lvdesk, musl, libSDL, libasound) and for everything else (PSRAM: all data, the 286 KB of .text..fast, and app text paged from SD). Re-run the h1s PC sampler at each point: if the user/kernel split moves with the clock, it says which half stalls. Two free riders: the 148 ms MSPI timing tuning has enormous margin at 100 MHz, so if the +-10% per-boot lottery collapses at the slow point the lottery is timing calibration; and a flat slope would kill an entire family of candidates in one afternoon rather than one build per hypothesis.
evidence: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/bootloader/sdkconfig:2721-2727 CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT, SPIRAM_SPEED_250M with 200M/100M/40M present; :1222-1230 FLASHFREQ_80M with 40M/20M present; :476-478 flash and PSRAM MSPI are independent controllers

The only existing datapoint of this shape was accidental and in the fast direction: DIO -> QIO doubled flash fetch bandwidth and CoreMark went +17% (dead-end register, 'Flash mode/clock as a lever'). Nobody has gone the other way as a control.

Arithmetic that says the pool is not small: artifacts/quake/h1s-062518 run.log is 969 frames in 56.6 s = 17.1 fps, and my resolve of pcs.txt puts 59% of CPU0 in user code. 0.59 x 320 MHz / 17.1 fps = 11.0 M cycles per frame for 76,800 pixels = 144 cycles/pixel, on a core that scores ~3.0 CoreMark/MHz (950-965 at 320 MHz) when its footprint fits in cache.

/Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/docs/accel-plan.md:42-50,114 in-cache memcpy 177 MB/s vs PSRAM 102, PPA 153, GDMA 210 - i.e. the bus ceiling is ~250 MB/s and the CPU copy already sits on it, while a dependent load costs 274.8-316 ns (worklog-2026-09-19.md:1609-1767).

Flash arithmetic that has never been checked against a workload: 22-32 MB/s measured (memory s31-flash-already-qio) makes a 64 B I-cache line ~600-900 cycles at 320 MHz, against ~100 cycles from PSRAM at 210 MB/s - which is exactly where the measured 5.98x comes from, and it has only ever been applied to 72 KB synthetic bodies.
magnitude_estimate: No direct gain: this is a bounding instrument. It prices C01 (autoload prefetch), C02 (critical-word-first), C05/C06 (AXI monitor and QoS), C21 (SRAM text tier), C23 (I-cache prelock), C32 (megapages), C39 (function-granular hot text), C68 (three-stream penalty), C74 (lent-CPU eviction) and C90 (library text in RAM) in one sweep, all of which are currently rated 'small' on argument rather than on a measured pool. Cost: 3 loader images, ~6 boots (2 per point for the lottery). If the Quake slope against PSRAM clock is flat, roughly a dozen candidates die at once; if run time moves 25-40% between 250 and 100 MHz, the memory-side family becomes the only place a large win can be.
rule_check: Passes. No application is rebuilt, relinked, configured or steered; apps stay on SD. Nothing is disabled - Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and sound all keep running, just against slower memory during the measurement. No mature upstream code is patched (the change is two Kconfig values in our own loader). Reversible by reflashing the loader; no NVS or other latched flash state is written, so the 'undo covers flash state' rule is satisfied.
prior_attempts: C03 and the round-2 'run the flash at 120 MHz' both tried to go FASTER and were blocked by silicon and by IDF having no S31 timing-tuning port. Going slower as a deliberate negative control has never been proposed or tried. cpufreq was found inert (hart0 holds 320 MHz; the hosted control message only raises the PM floor, bootloader/main/hosted_sram.c:499-545) and is the wrong axis anyway - the RISC-V timebase is declared as 320000000 in the DTS, so a CPU-clock arm breaks timekeeping unless the DTS and OpenSBI are rebuilt too, while the memory-clock arms leave the time base alone.

title: Measure the cache geometry, then pad-sweep the kernel text: every .text..fast result so far carries an uncontrolled layout variable
layer: kernel
mechanism: Nobody knows the associativity of either cache. IDF publishes sizes and line sizes only (16 KB I, 64 KB D, 64 B lines) and no WAYS field exists anywhere in the S31 soc_caps, cache_ll or Kconfig.cache. That matters because the one large, properly controlled result on this board that went the WRONG way is attributed to set aliasing and explicitly marked unproven: moving the 10 kB generic interrupt dispatch into RAM took the context switch from 107.8 to 171.3 us (+59%), reproduced by reverting to the byte-identical image. The linker script's own comment says the likely cause is that growing .text..fast moved the scheduler path into cache sets the interrupt path also occupies. If that is true, then the build's text layout is a hidden independent variable in every RAM-text experiment ever run here, and the whole spread of past results (-19.7%, -5%, -1.7%, +3.8%, +4%, +59%) may be layout, not fetch cost. Two-part instrument, no PMU needed: (a) geometry probe - execute k identical code copies placed at stride S, and separately read/write k data streams at stride S, sweeping S over 1-64 KB and k over 1-8; the k where throughput collapses gives the ways and the S gives the set stride, for the private I-cache and the shared D-cache. (b) layout probe - one '. += PAD;' before __text_fast_start in vmlinux-xip.lds.S, swept 0..8 KB in 64 B steps, measuring the context switch (ctxbench), pingpong and a Quake timedemo per build. The spread from padding alone is the size of the confound; the minimum of the curve is a win that costs zero RAM.
evidence: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/docs/current-state.md:5883-5918 - dispatch in RAM: cpubench idle 70.6 -> 72.4 M/s, under a download 40.5 -> 47.8, but context switch 107.8 -> 171.3 us, six settled runs each side, byte-identical revert restores 107.6. 'The mechanism is not established... aliasing rather than bandwidth... .text..fast is NOT a free win that scales.'

/Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/linux-71-port/arch/riscv/kernel/vmlinux-xip.lds.S:283 notes .text..fast is ordinary cached PSRAM competing for the D-cache, and :444-492 shows the section is one contiguous linker-controlled region - a single '. +=' is the whole knob.

/Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/images/System.map: __text_fast_start c083bc50, __text_fast_end c0881990 = 286,016 bytes of RAM text shipping today, all of it contending with hot flash text for the same 16 KB I-cache.

/Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/bootloader/sdkconfig:2819-2825 CACHE_L1_ICACHE_SIZE 0x4000, DCACHE 0x10000, both line 64 - and no associativity anywhere; ./docker/build.sh greps of /opt/esp-idf/components/hal/esp32s31/include/hal/cache_ll.h and soc_caps.h return nothing about ways.

C68 already assumes '2-way cache thrash' to explain the measured 18x three-stream write penalty - an assumption that has never been tested and that, if true, means three concurrent streams (texture read, framebuffer write, stack) collapse in exactly the loop shape the games run.
magnitude_estimate: Direct: a conflict-free layout is free RAM-wise and plausibly worth 1-3% of CPU0 (the switch is ~5% of CPU0 at 800 switches/s, and the one observed layout effect was 59% on the switch). Indirect and larger: it converts roughly twenty past null-or-noisy .text..fast results from 'measured, rejected' into 'measured under an uncontrolled variable', which is the only way C20/C21/C23/C39 get re-rated honestly. It also hands every future decision an exact stride for colouring platform buffers and hot text.
rule_check: Passes. Kernel linker-script change only; no application touched, nothing disabled, no upstream driver patched. The geometry probe is our own userspace binary. Costs no RAM (padding inside an existing section can be reclaimed by reordering once the minimum is known); must be verified in System.map per the .text..fast trap already recorded in memory.
prior_attempts: C39 orders hot functions by profile (density), which is about how much fits, not about which sets collide - and it would itself be measured under the same confound. C23 proposes the prelock hardware, a different mechanism. The +59% dispatch regression was correctly rejected but its mechanism was left unestablished and never probed. No associativity or stride measurement exists in any doc, artifact or rootfs tool.

title: Measure a kernel entry with the caches the game leaves behind: footprint-swept pingpong, and the victim-side refill tax
layer: kernel
mechanism: Every kernel-cost decision here was taken with pingpong or ctxbench, whose entire user side is a few hundred bytes, so both caches stay warm across the kernel entry. The real workload evicts a 16 KB private I-cache and most of a 64 KB shared D-cache between every entry. That is almost certainly why softirq.o measured -19.7% on pingpong while comparable object batches measured under 1% on Quake - the two ends of the decision were measured in different cache worlds, and the contradiction has never been reconciled. Instrument: a harness that puts a controlled footprint BETWEEN kernel entries - a generated straight-line/jump chain swept 0-64 KB (the ramtext generator already exists) plus a data sweep 0-256 KB - and plots syscall/futex round-trip cost against footprint, run on the shipping kernel and on a kernel with more of the spine in RAM. The second half, which nobody has ever measured on this board, is the victim side: hold the footprint fixed and vary the injected interrupt rate (timerfd, or the existing touch idle_poll_ms knob at 669 vs 125/s) and measure the user loop's throughput slope. That slope is microseconds of user time destroyed per interrupt - a cost that every profile taken here charges to user code, because the samples land in the game while it refills its own cache.
evidence: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/rootfs/pingpong.c header: two threads, a futex and nothing else - by construction the warmest possible cache state, and it is the instrument that justified the second-biggest past win.

My resolve of /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/artifacts/quake/h1s-062518/pcs.txt (12,000 samples) split at __text_fast_start: kernel 40.3% of CPU0, of which idle (arch_cpu_idle, flash-resident) 8.6%; kernel code still executing from XIP flash is 19.8% of CPU0 and the 286 KB already in RAM is 11.8%. Neither number appears in any doc.

Same resolve, by subsystem: irq/entry 6.30%, scheduler 5.06%, timers 4.18% = 15.5% of CPU0 on interrupt and scheduling machinery during a fullscreen game; the rest of the kernel is a flat tail (top unbucketed symbol is __radix_tree_lookup at 0.17%).

The warm/cold split is already visible in the dead-end register and was read as a null: footprintbench 33.14 vs 32.66 ns/call and lvdesk HOTTEXT 23.1/23.5 vs 24.3 fps (hot loops that FIT the I-cache, so RAM text cannot help), against ramtext '41 KB straight-line is 4.8x' (a path that refetches itself, which is what a kernel entry does).

Cost arithmetic: a 64 B line is ~600-900 cycles from 22-32 MB/s flash and ~100 from PSRAM, so refilling 4 KB of cold entry path is ~38-58k cycles = 120-180 us; at the measured event rates (227 timer IRQs/s plus 165-804 context switches/s, docs/smp-finish-plan.md:154-158 and docs/current-state.md:5859) that is a double-digit share of the core if the path really is cold each time - and nothing on this board has ever tested whether it is.
magnitude_estimate: Instrument, over a pool of 19.8% of CPU0 (kernel code executing from flash) with irq+sched+timers alone at 15.5%. If the in-situ entry cost turns out to be 3-5x what pingpong reports, then recovering even a third of the flash-resident kernel time is +5-8% fps and C20/C21/C23/C39 stop being 'small'; if the cold and warm numbers agree, the entire RAM-text family is honestly closed for the first time and the review can stop paying for it. Either outcome is worth more than another build-per-hypothesis arm.
rule_check: Passes. The harness is our own binary; Quake/Doom are not rebuilt, relinked or steered, and stay on SD. Nothing is disabled. The A/B kernels are our own port, not upstream code. The touch-poll knob used as an interrupt-rate lever is an existing runtime module parameter, preferred over a rebuild per the standing rule.
prior_attempts: pingpong, ctxbench, footprintbench, ramtext and locktext all exist and none of them varies the user footprint BETWEEN kernel entries; footprintbench measures call cost with the footprint resident, not the eviction. The touch-poll rate change (timer 669 -> 125-154/s) was reported as 'busy ticks unchanged' with no noise floor and no victim-side measurement, which is a null that cannot distinguish 'no tax' from 'tax below a +-10% lottery'.

title: A wake ledger in the scheduler: who sleeps, for how long, and who woke them - Quake's unattributed 10% and the ~800 switches/s
layer: scheduler-ipc
mechanism: The project's own ceiling analysis says the 20 fps goal IS Quake's waits (86% busy -> 17.3/0.84 = 20.6 fps), and the project's own instrument then failed to attribute the largest part of them: waitsamp reports 'short sleeps (under a few ms, which read running by the time /proc/<tid>/syscall is read) make ~10%'. A 1 kHz sampler cannot see a sub-millisecond sleep, so the conclusion 'no single wait is worth chasing' rests on a 10% hole. Sampling cannot fix this; accounting can. Add a small scheduler-side ledger: on dequeue record (task, current syscall nr or fault type, ktime); on wake record the waker's pid and the sleep duration into a per-task log2 histogram; expose it through /proc or a fixed-size ring dumped after a run. That is ~30 lines in __schedule/try_to_wake_up and a few hundred bytes per task. It answers four questions at once that nothing here can answer today: how many wakeups a Quake frame actually costs and to whom, what the 15.5% of CPU0 in irq+sched+timers is the numerator of, which of the ~800 switches/s are platform-to-platform (lvdesk, the xlite ring, s31route, kworkers - all our code, both ends) and which are unavoidable, and whether the 10% of short sleeps is one wait repeated 30 times a frame or noise spread thin.
evidence: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/docs/smp-finish-plan.md:149-153 - waitsamp: running 86%, short sleeps ~10% unattributed, faults ~2%, ppoll 1.8%; and :138-141 'the ceiling is removing Quake's waits: 17.3 / 0.84 = 20.6 fps'.

/Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/docs/current-state.md:5859 - measured switch rates 165 (idle) / 460 (drag) / 804 (busiest) per second at 107.8 us per switch, i.e. 1.2% of the core per 100 switches/s; combined with my resolve of the Quake profile (scheduler 5.06% + irq/entry 6.30% of CPU0) that implies several hundred switches/s during the timedemo, and nobody has ever listed the pairs.

docs/smp-finish-plan.md:154-158 - 227 timer interrupts/s under Quake, with hrtimer_wakeup, tick_nohz_handler, hrtick, dl_task_timer and our vblank tick all in timer_list, and hw_vblank measured inert: the rate is known, the wake SOURCES are not.

The shape has already paid once: late present (+13% Doom, 34.6 -> 39.1 fps) was exactly a frame-handoff restructuring, and it was found structurally rather than measured - there was no instrument that could have pointed at it.

/Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/docs/current-state.md:4759-4774 shows the current best effort - voluntary_ctxt_switches counts and an inference of '~11 hrtimer expiries and context switches per poll' - counts with no reasons and no wakers.
magnitude_estimate: Instrument over two pools: Quake's own 10% of unattributed waits (directly on the path to the 20 fps goal, which is a 17% gap from 17.1 fps) and the 11.4% of CPU0 in scheduler plus entry. It prices C43 (poll-before-wfi), C44 (ring spin-then-sleep), C30 (tick duty to CPU1), C34 (vblank hrtimer) and C42 (HRTICK) with a measured wake count instead of an estimate, and it is the only way to find a late-present-shaped restructuring deliberately rather than by luck.
rule_check: Passes. Kernel-side only, in our own port; no application is modified, wrapped or steered - which is precisely why the hook has to be in the scheduler rather than in an LD_PRELOAD. Nothing disabled. Cost is a few hundred bytes per task behind a config, and the ledger does no work when not being read, so it can ship off and be built in for a measurement kernel (DIAG-style), keeping the 15.4 MB constraint intact.
prior_attempts: waitsamp (rootfs/waitsamp.c) samples /proc/<tid>/syscall and is blind below a few ms by its own account; h1s samples PCs at 1 kHz and only on CPU0; /proc/PID/status gives counts without reasons; ftrace, perf and the PMU do not exist here. The scheduler tunables that were swept (RUN_TO_PARITY, base_slice_ns, DELAY_DEQUEUE, preemption model) were all tuned blind, without knowing what the wakeups were.

title: A legal stand-in for the app's inner loop: a rasterizer-shaped working-set sweep, alone, with a co-runner, and against the scanout DMA
layer: cross-layer
mechanism: The app may not be touched, so the only way to get a derivative of 'frame time vs locality' is a stand-in with the same access shape. Every memory instrument on this board measures sequential streaming or one pointer chase, at a fixed size, on one hart, with no DMA running - which is the one access pattern a texture-mapped span loop does not have. Build spanbench: 8-bit texture reads stepping u,v down a span with a power-of-two row pitch, writing a 320x240 8-bit target, sweeping the texture working set from 4 KB to 4 MB and the row pitch across the conflict stride found by the geometry probe, reporting cycles/pixel. Then repeat under the three contention conditions that actually hold during a timedemo: the other hart running lvdesk's real present loop, the LCD scanout on and off, and the PSRAM clock arms. That decomposes the 144 cycles/pixel Quake actually achieves into capacity misses, conflict misses and cross-agent contention - three different fixes, all platform-side (physical page colouring of the game's anonymous pages, buffer placement for the SHM segment and scanout, keeping CPU1's streaming work out of the shared D-cache), and today indistinguishable.
evidence: Quake's user-mode budget from artifacts/quake/h1s-062518: 0.59 x 320 MHz / 17.1 fps = 11.0 M cycles per frame for 76,800 pixels = 144 cycles/pixel, on a core that does ~3.0 CoreMark/MHz with a cache-resident footprint. The gap is roughly an order of magnitude and has never been decomposed.

/Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/rootfs/membw.c header: 2 MB fixed, streaming plus one pointer chase, single hart, no DMA - explicitly built to answer a per-boot question, not a locality one. membench compares SRAM vs PSRAM for the same two patterns.

The D-cache is 64 KB and shared by both harts (and the scanout, PPA and GDMA traffic sits on the same bus): bootloader/sdkconfig:2821, plus accel-plan.md:42-50,114 (CPU 102, PPA 153, GDMA 210 MB/s against 177 in-cache).

Bandwidth has already been eliminated as the constraint, which is what leaves latency and conflict: dropping the panel 59 -> 35 Hz removed 18.4 MB/s of continuous scanout (45.3 -> 26.9) and fps did not move (docs/current-state.md:680-702).
C74 argues the lent CPU evicts the game's working set and C68 argues a three-stream conflict, and neither has an instrument; the 18x three-stream penalty is a measured fact with no measured cause.
magnitude_estimate: Instrument. It cannot win anything by itself, but it is the only way to turn proposal 1's single global number into a choice of fix, and the only way to price C74 without a PMU. If conflict or co-runner contention turns out to be a third of the 144 cycles/pixel, then page colouring and buffer placement - both free, both platform-side, both currently unpriced - become the largest untried levers on the user-mode 59% that the hard rules otherwise put out of reach.
rule_check: Passes. spanbench is our own benchmark; Quake, Doom and OpenTyrian are not rebuilt, relinked, reconfigured or steered, and nothing about the app's own layout is changed by measuring it. Apps stay on SD. Nothing disabled. Runs entirely in userspace on the shipping kernel for the single-hart arms.
prior_attempts: blitbench, clutbench, pixbench, blendbench and expbench all measure copies, fills and palette expansion - the present path, not a texture-mapped read; membw and membench measure streaming and chase only. The round-2 memory-level-parallelism idea asks how many misses can be outstanding on a streaming pattern; this asks what the miss RATE and conflict behaviour are at app-shaped strides and footprints, and adds the two contention axes (co-runner, DMA) that no memory measurement here has ever included.

title: 16 KiB is free on this card and every file fault asks for 4: give SD-backed page cache a minimum folio order
layer: kernel mm/page cache + arch/riscv + ext4 (linux-71-port/include/linux/pgtable.h, mm/filemap.c, mm/readahead.c, fs/ext4/super.c)
mechanism:
The card's cost is FLAT below 16 KiB — sdlat p50, random, n=200: 1k 2.25, 2k 2.20, 4k 2.25, 8k 2.36, 16k 2.51, 32k 3.00 ms — and the minimum barely moves under a full-core spinner (1.99 -> 2.09 ms), so it is a per-transaction hardware floor, not software. current-state.md already draws the conclusion ('the lever is request size, not code placement', 6 MB as 4 KiB faults = 3.4 s vs 256 KiB reads = 0.18 s, 19x) but only ever applied it to the readahead WINDOW. The UNIT was never touched: every page-cache folio for an SD-backed file on this board is order 0, so every file-backed major fault is a 4 KiB bio that pays 2.25 ms to move 4 KiB when 16 KiB would have cost 2.51.

Three code sites hold it at order 0, and all three are ours to change:
(1) include/linux/pgtable.h:579-588 — the generic exec_folio_order() returns 0 and riscv does not override it (arm64 overrides it to get contpte-mapped text). mm/filemap.c:3376-3398 feeds that straight into ra->order for every VM_EXEC mapping.
(2) mm/filemap.c:3400-3408 — the non-exec 'mmap read-around' branch hardcodes ra->order = 0. That is the branch prboom's 4 MB mmapped WAD and every mmapped data file takes.
(3) fs/ext4/super.c:5223 sets s_min_folio_order = get_order(blocksize) = 0 for 4 KiB blocks, so mapping_min_folio_order() is 0 and mm/readahead.c's page_cache_ra_order() clamps with new_order = max(new_order, 0).

What the machine already supports and nobody used: without THP, include/linux/pagemap.h:377-387 sets PREFERRED_MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER = 8, so MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER = 8 — large PAGE-CACHE folios are available on this rv32 kernel even though large ANON folios (mTHP) are not. ext4 here already advertises up to that (fs/ext4/super.c:5091-5101, EXT4_MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER = umin(MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, 11); fs/ext4/inode.c:5203-5220 calls mapping_set_folio_order_range on every regular inode). The capability is wired up and the order is pinned to 0 at the two arch/policy sites above.

Setting the unit to order 2 (16 KiB) makes four things happen at once in the unit the device charges for: the I/O becomes one 16 KiB bio; filemap_map_pages installs all 4 PTEs from one folio instead of 4 separate minor faults; the LRU carries 1 entry instead of 4; and reclaim EVICTS 16 KiB as a unit, so the refault is also one 16 KiB read. The fourth is the one readahead can never give, because it survives the readahead heuristics being switched off (see the companion mmap_miss proposal).

Two implementation forms, in increasing risk: (a) safe — define exec_folio_order() = 2 for riscv and set ra->order = 2 in the read-around branch. page_cache_ra_order()/ra_alloc_folio() degrade gracefully: a failed order-2 allocation breaks the loop and falls back to do_page_cache_ra() at order 0. (b) strong — set ext4's s_min_folio_order to 2 on this board, which also covers the bare fault path (mm/filemap.c:2612-2618, 4076 allocate at mapping_min_folio_order), at the cost that an order-2 allocation failure under fragmentation is an error rather than a fallback. Measure (a) first; it is a three-line change and a single kernel build.
evidence: docs/current-state.md:2003-2008 — sdlat p50 random n=200: 1k 2.25 / 2k 2.20 / 4k 2.25 / 8k 2.36 / 16k 2.51 / 32k 3.00 ms; under a full-core spinner p50 rises 2.25->2.93 but the MINIMUM only 1.99->2.09, i.e. the floor is the card, not us
docs/current-state.md:2030-2040 — 'The lever is request size, not code placement': 6 MB as 4 KiB faults = 1536 x 2.2 ms = 3.4 s, as 256 KiB reads = 24 x 7.6 ms = 0.18 s (19x)

linux-71-port/include/linux/pgtable.h:579-588 — exec_folio_order() default returns 0; no riscv override anywhere in the tree (grep over include/, mm/, arch/riscv/ finds only pgtable.h and filemap.c:3393)
linux-71-port/mm/filemap.c:3376-3398 — VM_EXEC branch: ra->order = exec_folio_order(); ra->size = ra_pages rounded to that order; async_size = 0
linux-71-port/mm/filemap.c:3400-3408 — mmap read-around branch: ra->order = 0 hardcoded

linux-71-port/include/linux/pagemap.h:377-387 — PREFERRED_MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER = 8 when !THP; MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER = min(MAX_XAS_ORDER, 8). Large page-cache folios are NOT gated on THP, unlike anon/mTHP
linux-71-port/fs/ext4/super.c:5091-5101 and :5223 — s_max_folio_order = umin(MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, 11); s_min_folio_order = get_order(4096) = 0
linux-71-port/fs/ext4/inode.c:5203-5220 — ext4_set_inode_mapping_order() calls mapping_set_folio_order_range() for every regular inode, so the mechanism is already live per-file
linux-71-port/mm/readahead.c page_cache_ra_order() — new_order = min(mapping_max_folio_order, ra->order) then max(new_order, min_order); with both inputs 0 every readahead folio is order 0

artifacts/quake/td-lot-1-073524/run.log — 969 frames 59.8 s 16.2 fps, majflt=1282, VmRSS 4916 kB, VmSwap 6132 kB, MemAvailable 316 kB (the whole paging envelope: 1282 x 3.3 ms = 4.2 s of 59.8 s = 7.1%)
docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:258-262 — slow seconds of a Doom demo carry 2x the SD reads (345 vs 168 KB/s) and 2x the game's major faults: 'The game pages its text and WAD lumps off the card mid-demo'

buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/overlay/etc/init.d/S02s31-blockdev — the whole documented readahead history is window sizes (16/32/64/128/256/512/1024 kB); the folio/allocation unit is never mentioned
magnitude_estimate: Bounded above by the file-backed share of Quake's 1,282 major faults. The entire paging tax on the headline metric is 1,282 x 3.3 ms = 4.2 s of a 59.8 s demo = 7.1% (16.2 -> 17.4 fps if every fault vanished), and this proposal only addresses the file-backed half, whose size is currently unmeasured. Realistic: +1-3% on Quake (16.2 -> 16.4-16.7 fps). Larger and more visible on prboom, which mmaps a 4 MB WAD it can never cache (97-314 major faults per 30-60 s in the S02s31-blockdev sweep) and whose measured hitching was attributed to exactly these faults. Also cuts launch for any SD-resident binary, where text is faulted in cold. This is a 'small' by the review's own scale and I am not going to call it anything else.
rule_check: PASSES. No application code, binary, link, config or wrapper is touched — the change is in our kernel. Apps stay on the SD card and still page from it; this changes only the size of the request the kernel makes to the card. Nothing is disabled: no Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or feature is traded. It is not a patch to Xorg, mesa or dwc2; it is a 3-line arch/policy change in mm/filemap.c plus a riscv exec_folio_order() definition, in a tree that already carries 58 kernel patches including sched/fair and dw_mmc. Memory cost is the risk, not the rule: a 16 KiB minimum wastes up to 12 KiB per sparsely-touched page on a board with 316 kB free, which is why 16 KiB (the exact flat point) and not 64 or 128 KiB is the number, and why form (a) with graceful order-0 fallback is measured first.
prior_attempts: The readahead WINDOW has been swept repeatedly and the results are recorded in S02s31-blockdev (16/32/64/128/256/512/1024 kB, with 128 kB shipping and 1024 kB a cliff) — every arm moved how MUCH is read ahead, none moved the allocation/eviction unit. fault_around (64 KiB, mm/memory.c:5824-5870) only maps pages already in the cache and issues no I/O, and its knob is debugfs-only so DIAG=0 compiles it out (current-state.md:2033-2038). C92 ('batch exec-time text paging through ld.so MADV_WILLNEED, expose fault_around_bytes') was refuted — a userspace hint, not the kernel's request unit. Dead-end register #90 says 'Folios off without THP', which is true for ANON folios (mTHP needs 64BIT on riscv, mm/Kconfig) and false for page-cache folios (pagemap.h:377-387); that conflation is what has kept this closed. C32 ('4 MB megapages for the RV32 linear map') is the kernel's own linear map, a different mapping entirely. None of the 95 existing candidates names folio order for user file pages.

title: Memory pressure permanently switches OFF file readahead for the game's mappings — the mmap_miss ratchet, and one ra_pages doing two incompatible jobs
layer: kernel mm/filemap.c readahead policy (MMAP_LOTSAMISS ratchet) + the bdi ra_pages split
mechanism:
mm/filemap.c:3346-3357: every mmap fault that misses the page cache increments f_ra.mmap_miss, and once mmap_miss > MMAP_LOTSAMISS (100, filemap.c:3258) do_sync_mmap_readahead() returns immediately — readahead is off for that file for the rest of the mapping's life. The only thing that decrements it is filemap_map_pages() finding folios ALREADY CACHED (filemap.c:3941-3957: mmap_miss_saved is reduced only by the count of pages fault-around actually mapped).

On a board with 316 kB free that is a positive feedback loop with a latch. Pages are not cached, so every fault is a miss, so mmap_miss ratchets to its ceiling (it is allowed to climb to MMAP_LOTSAMISS*10 = 1000 before it stops counting), so readahead switches off, so every subsequent refault is a bare 4 KiB request at the 2.25 ms floor, so still nothing is cached. The heuristic is designed for 'this file is being accessed randomly, readahead will only hurt' on a device where a bigger read costs proportionally more. On THIS device a 4 KiB read and a 16 KiB read cost the same (2.25 vs 2.51 ms), so 'readahead will only hurt' is false for any window up to 16 KiB, and the kernel has no way to know that. This is the most economical explanation I can find for the measured behaviour 'the game pages its text and WAD lumps off the card mid-demo' costing full price per page, and it bites hardest exactly when it hurts most.

Second, separable defect at the same site: f_ra.ra_pages is a single number (bdi->ra_pages, written by read_ahead_kb at block/blk-sysfs.c:206, copied per-file by file_ra_state_init) that serves two jobs with opposite optima. As the SEQUENTIAL window for read() it wants to be large — the sweep in S02s31-blockdev found 128 kB and 512 kB good for streaming. As the mmap READ-AROUND size (filemap.c:3404-3406: ra->size = ra->ra_pages centred on the fault) it wants to be ~16-32 kB, because on a memory-poor board a 128 kB read-around evicts 128 kB to deliver 4 kB. The sweep documented this collision without naming it: for prboom's mmapped WAD, '128 kB is beaten on BOTH axes by both 32 and 64' (101 faults / 5.0 MB at 64 kB against 120 faults / 9.4 MB at 128 kB), and 1024 kB was a catastrophic cliff (336 faults). The fix is to stop making one knob arbitrate two curves.

Three candidate changes, each independently A/B-able with no userspace change: (i) make the ratchet size-aware — when readahead has been disabled by mmap_miss, still do a MINIMUM read-around of 16 KiB, which is free on this device and can only reduce faults; (ii) decay mmap_miss on a time or fault-count basis so a mapping that misses during a load phase is not condemned for the rest of the process; (iii) give mmap read-around its own size, independent of bdi->ra_pages, exposed as a sysctl so the two curves can be swept separately on one boot.
evidence: linux-71-port/mm/filemap.c:3258 — #define MMAP_LOTSAMISS (100)

linux-71-port/mm/filemap.c:3346-3357 — mmap_miss is incremented on every miss (up to MMAP_LOTSAMISS*10) and 'if (mmap_miss > MMAP_LOTSAMISS) return fpin;' disables read-around entirely, ahead of both the VM_EXEC and the read-around branches

linux-71-port/mm/filemap.c:3936-3957 — filemap_map_pages() decrements mmap_miss only by the number of already-cached folios it managed to map; under pressure there are none, so the counter never comes down
linux-71-port/mm/filemap.c:3404-3406 — read-around size is exactly ra->ra_pages, i.e. the same number as the sequential read window
linux-71-port/block/blk-sysfs.c:206 and linux-71-port/mm/backing-dev.c:272 — read_ahead_kb writes the single bdi->ra_pages that both paths read

buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/overlay/etc/init.d/S02s31-blockdev — measured for prboom's mmapped WAD: 16 kB 314 faults/15,336 sectors; 32 kB 141/8,968; 64 kB 101/10,296; 128 kB 120/19,296; 256 kB 97/24,712. '128 kB is beaten on BOTH axes by both 32 and 64.' The same file says 512 KB was chosen earlier because it 'measured slightly better for a sequential read (11.8 against 8.3 MB/s)' — the two curves, in one knob
docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:258-262 — slow seconds of a windowed Doom demo carry 2x SD reads and 2x the game's major faults; 'The game pages its text and WAD lumps off the card mid-demo'
docs/current-state.md:2003-2008 — the 4 KiB/16 KiB cost equality that makes the heuristic's premise false here
artifacts/quake/td-lot-1-073524/run.log — majflt=1282 with MemAvailable 316 kB, i.e. the process runs its whole life on the wrong side of the latch
magnitude_estimate: Same 7.1% ceiling as any paging change on Quake (1,282 x 3.3 ms of a 59.8 s demo), and again only the file-backed share of it. Expect +0.5-2% on Quake. The better target is prboom, where the fault population IS the mmapped WAD and the sweep already shows a 20% fault-count spread (101 vs 120 vs 314) purely from window size — a 16 KiB always-on minimum should beat every arm in that table on both axes at once, since it is the only point that reduces faults without increasing sectors read. Also improves launch of any SD-resident binary whose text faults in scattered order past 100 misses. If (iii) is implemented, the immediate return is that the read_ahead_kb sweep can finally be run as two separate sweeps instead of one compromise.
rule_check: PASSES. Kernel-side only; no app is rebuilt, relinked, reconfigured or wrapped; apps stay on SD and page from SD, and this makes each of those pages cheaper rather than moving them. No feature disabled. mm/filemap.c is core upstream code, but the changes are a constant, a decay and an extra sysctl, not a rewrite of a mature driver of the Xorg/mesa/dwc2 class, and this tree already carries kernel patches in mm-adjacent and scheduler code. Memory risk is bounded by construction: the always-on minimum is 16 KiB, chosen as the device's flat point, and it is strictly smaller than today's 128 KiB read-around whenever that one runs.
prior_attempts: Never examined. The project's entire readahead history (S02s31-blockdev, current-state.md:8270-8288) is sweeps of read_ahead_kb, i.e. of the value the heuristic multiplies — never of whether the heuristic was running at all. Dead-end #66 ('fps dips are swap / page-cache warming / readahead as a Quake lever') closed the WINDOW as a lever and explicitly recorded 'Quake's faults are heap swap, not readahead', which is a claim about which LRU the faults come from and says nothing about the file faults that do happen. C92 (ld.so MADV_WILLNEED + expose fault_around_bytes, refuted) attacks the same symptom from userspace with a different mechanism and does not touch mmap_miss. fault_around_bytes is a different knob on a different path (it maps cached pages, it issues no I/O) and is compiled out by DIAG=0 anyway. No entry in the 95-candidate index or the 98-entry dead-end register mentions mmap_miss, MMAP_LOTSAMISS, or the ra_pages double duty.

title: Back the game's 10 MB heap with a file instead of swap: musl's large-allocation path is platform code and swap-in is the one I/O path on this board that can never be batched
layer: platform libc (musl 1.2.6 mallocng, already patched in this toolchain) + kernel mm consequences
mechanism:
Quake's heap is one malloc() far above musl mallocng's mmap threshold (~128 KiB), so it becomes a single MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS mapping, lands on the anon LRU, and is paged to /swapfile on the card. That backing store is the worst one available here, for a reason that is structural rather than tunable:

- The swap-OUT path is already batched. mm/vmscan.c:5955-6025 wraps shrink_lruvec in a blk_plug, so folios reclaimed into consecutive slots merge into large writes.
- The swap-IN path cannot be. With vm.page-cluster = 0 (99-s31-memory.conf, measured and deliberate), swap_vma_ra_win() returns 1 (mm/swap_state.c:759-761), swap_vma_readahead() jumps to 'skip', and the fault issues exactly one unplugged 4 KiB bio (mm/swap_state.c:822-830). There is nothing to merge it with, because a demand fault is by definition alone.
- Turning readahead on does not fix the shape, only the size, and the two available modes are mutually exclusive in the wrong way: VMA mode (mm/swap_state.c:800-830) gives VA locality but issues N separate bios at scattered slots — N x 2.25 ms; PHYSICAL mode (mm/swap_state.c:698-750) gives one merged request but orders by swap slot, not by virtual address. Neither gives 'VA-local AND one request', because a swap slot number is not a heap offset.

A file mapping gives both for free, because file offset IS virtual offset. If musl's mallocng serves allocations at/above its mmap threshold with a MAP_SHARED mapping over a sparse file on the ext4 root instead of MAP_ANONYMOUS, then: (i) filemap readahead is VA-local by construction and merges into one request; (ii) fault-around installs up to 16 PTEs per fault from the cache (mm/memory.c:5843-5870); (iii) the folio-order lever from the companion proposal applies to the heap too, so the eviction and refault unit becomes 16 KiB; (iv) writeback clusters contiguous dirty pages by file offset; (v) the heap becomes addressable from OUTSIDE the process as a file — posix_fadvise/readahead()/MADV_PAGEOUT on an fd — which is the only concrete handle the sweep's 'can the compositor prefetch a known working set' question has ever been offered.

Second-order effect worth as much as the first: it repairs the swappiness dilemma. Today the file LRU is 'XIP flash text (free to re-read) plus the game's SD text', and the anon LRU is 'the game's 10 MB heap plus the daemons', so no global vm.swappiness is right — 99-s31-memory.conf documents the value being flipped 100 -> 10 for exactly this reason and the flip is now wrong for SD-resident games. With the heap on the file LRU, the file LRU is essentially 'the foreground game' and the anon LRU is essentially 'the background daemons', and swappiness becomes a clean foreground/background dial instead of a compromise.

Risks, stated plainly: MAP_SHARED changes fork and MADV_DONTNEED semantics for mallocng — freed-and-reused memory must still read as zeros for calloc, so frees of large chunks must punch holes (FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE) rather than rely on fresh-mmap zeroing; ext4 writeback per dirty page is heavier than a raw swap extent; and the backing file must be created and unlinked cleanly per process. Gate it behind an env knob read by musl (set by lvdesk's launcher) so it is opt-in and reversible at runtime, or make it musl's unconditional behaviour above the threshold if a reviewer reads the per-program env knob as steering the app.
evidence: linux-71-port/mm/swap_state.c:759-761 — swap_vma_ra_win(): 'max_win = 1 << min(page_cluster, SWAP_RA_ORDER_CEILING); if (max_win == 1) return 1;' — with page-cluster 0 there is no swap readahead at all
linux-71-port/mm/swap_state.c:822-830 — the 'skip' path: one swap_cache_alloc_folio + swap_read_folio(folio, NULL), no plug, one 4 KiB bio per major fault

linux-71-port/mm/swap_state.c:698-750 vs :800-830 — cluster readahead plugs consecutive SLOTS (merges into one big request, wrong order); vma readahead walks the PTEs around the fault (right order, N scattered bios)
linux-71-port/mm/vmscan.c:5955-6025 — blk_start_plug around the whole shrink_lruvec scan loop: the write side already merges, so the read side is the only unbatched half

buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/overlay/etc/sysctl.d/99-s31-memory.conf — vm.page-cluster = 0 (measured, with the reasoning); vm.swappiness = 10 with the explicit premise 'a file page evicted now costs a cheap re-read from memory-mapped flash' — a premise that is false for a game whose text, WAD and pak are on SD
docs/current-state.md:1972-1974 — swap-in from the SD swapfile measures 1.18 MB/s, ~3.3 ms/page (swapbench, 12 MB in 10.20 s) against a 2.25 ms device floor: ~1.05 ms per fault is ours

docs/current-state.md:1963-1967 — 'mmap() does not pay it. A file-backed fault inserts the page-cache page into the process page tables with no copy, so demand paging runs at SD speed. Prefer mmap over read for anything sized in megabytes in code we control.'

artifacts/quake/td-lot-1-073524/run.log — VmSwap 6132 kB against VmRSS 4916 kB and majflt 1282: ~5 MB faulted back one page at a time over a 59.8 s demo, i.e. a slow one-time reload, not thrash (each swapped page faults ~0.85 times)

buildroot/package/musl/musl.mk — MUSL_VERSION = 1.2.6, i.e. mallocng; docs/xespv-libc.md:1-20 — the toolchain already carries a RISC-V-specific musl patch, so patching musl is established practice here, not a new capability

CHECK BEFORE BUILDING: confirm mallocng's threshold and single-mmap behaviour in musl 1.2.6 src/malloc/mallocng/malloc.c (MMAP_THRESHOLD, the 'if (n >= MMAP_THRESHOLD)' branch) and confirm TyrQuake's heap is one malloc — the -mem 12/10/9 arms in current-state.md:6712-6717 and 'the default 128 MB heap cannot start' in scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh both imply it is
magnitude_estimate: Ceiling is the whole paging tax: 1,282 major faults x 3.3 ms = 4.2 s of a 59.8 s demo = 7.1%, i.e. 16.2 -> 17.4 fps if every fault disappeared, which it will not. A 2-4x batching of the swap-backed share is +2-4% (16.2 -> 16.5-16.9 fps). It does NOT reach the 20 fps goal and it is not in the class of SMP / .text..fast / the lvdesk layer collapse; say so. Worth noting what this sweep also establishes negatively, because it bounds everything else in this area: the faulted-back set is ~5 MB read roughly once each, so this is a capacity problem, not a thrash problem, and no predictor or prefetcher can help — there is nowhere to put a prefetched page with 316 kB free. And the reachable 'reshape who holds memory' pool is small: total userspace RSS with everything in XIP is ~1.8 MB (current-state.md:3331), so pre-evicting the entire desktop buys the game at most ~1 MB, i.e. under 1%.
rule_check: PASSES, with one grey edge named. musl libc is explicitly listed as platform side ('the shared libraries apps load dynamically (SDL1.2, SDL2, musl libc/ld.so, libasound)'), the app is not rebuilt, relinked, reconfigured or wrapped, and no app-visible config is steered — the env knob steers OUR allocator, not Quake. The grey edge: a per-program env var set by the launcher could be read as config-steering; the clean alternative is to make it musl's default for every allocation above the threshold, which removes the ambiguity at the cost of applying it machine-wide. The app's code and data stay on the SD card and page from it — more of it does, in larger units. Nothing is disabled. No mature upstream code is patched (musl's malloc is ours to change and is already patched in this toolchain).
prior_attempts: The alternatives to SD swap have all been tried and all failed for the same reason: zram four times across three eras (24 MB, 4 MB, 512 kB mem_limit — 'a compressed copy of RAM in RAM is not a saving here', etc/s31-swap.conf), zswap (C48, refuted), MGLRU (needs 64BIT/FLATMEM), THP and mTHP (64BIT-only on riscv), hugetlbfs (pins 12 MB), a raw swap partition (equals a swapfile on the same stack). Every one of those kept the heap ANONYMOUS and changed where the anonymous pages went. Not one moved the heap off the anon LRU. The page-cluster sweeps (dead-end #33, C49, and the round-1/round-2 'switch swap-in to physical-slot readahead' items) tune the swap readahead mode and are the right thing to try first — they are also the arms that will tell you which half of the 1,282 faults is swap, which this proposal needs. Dead-end #90 rejected 'huge pages for heaps' and 'a CPU1 prefetch daemon' on reasoning; neither is this. C55 and the round-1 'pre-evict the idle platform set with process_madvise(MADV_PAGEOUT)' reshape who holds memory but leave the backing store alone, and the ~1.8 MB total userspace RSS bounds what they can return.

title: Price CPU0's interrupt entries at ~170 us each and delete the 136/s that have no consumer
layer: kernel: drivers/gpu/drm/espressif/esp32s31-lcd.c, esp32s31-ppa.c, plus one kernel command-line word (Makefile CMDLINE_ADD)
mechanism: The per-interrupt cost on this board is set by how many bytes of XIP kernel text the entry path touches, not by what the handler does, because Quake owns the 16 KB private I-cache between interrupts. Two independent derivations agree: (a) IRQ/CLIC/entry is 6.4% of CPU0 and the measured interrupt rate is 371/s, giving 172 us per entry; (b) sizing the common entry chain from images/System.map -- handle_exception 248 + do_irq 80 + call_on_irq_stack 64 + handle_riscv_irq 62 + esp32s31_clic_handle_irq 378 + generic_handle_domain_irq 24 + __irq_resolve_mapping 88 + handle_irq_desc 58 + handle_level_irq 114 / handle_percpu_devid_irq 244 + __handle_irq_event_percpu 426 + handle_irq_event 142 + add_interrupt_randomness 162 + fast_mix 132 + note_interrupt 432 + mask/unmask/ack 166 + irq_can_handle 30 + set_irq_regs 50 + irqentry_enter 54 + part of irqentry_exit + ret_from_exception 114 -- is ~3.2 KB = 50 cache lines, and 64 B from QIO-80 flash at the measured 22-32 MB/s is ~2.7 us, so 50 lines = ~135 us, leaving ~35 us of actual execution. A third cross-check: esp32s31_clic_handle_irq alone is 0.78% of CPU0 = 21 us per call for a 378-byte (6-line) function, i.e. 3.5 us/line. So interrupt COUNT is the budget, and four groups of interrupts currently cost 170 us each while doing nothing a consumer reads: (1) esp32s31-lcd.c:1778 enables LCD_INT_MASK (VSYNC|TRANS_DONE|UNDERRUN) unconditionally at pipe enable, but the ISR at :2442 acts on VSYNC/TRANS_DONE only when hw_vblank is set, and hw_vblank defaults false (:554) -- measured 52 IRQ/s during Quake that only increment debug counters; (2) esp32s31-lcd.c:1783 starts the emulated-vblank hrtimer unconditionally for as long as the pipe is on (refcounting deliberately abandoned), ~42/s, but prompt_flip defaults true (:549) so flips are never armed against vblank, and lvdesk contains no WAIT_VBLANK, no PAGE_FLIP and no libdrm vblank use at all -- it drives KMS with SETCRTC+DIRTYFB -- so nothing consumes the vblank; (3) esp32s31-ppa.c spins up to ppa_spin_us=300 on DMA2D_IN_SUC_EOF (:583-:600) and its own comment says 'If the spin wins, the ISR still runs and still completes ->done' -- the PPA EOF and 2D-DMA EOF interrupts (19/s + 23/s measured) are redundant by construction whenever the spin wins, which it does at ~169 us per op; (4) note_interrupt is 432 bytes, 13% of the whole entry path, fetched on every one of the 371/s on CPU0 and 197/s on CPU1, and is disabled outright by the stock `noirqdebug` boot parameter (kernel/irq/manage.c:1751 sets the per-desc no_debug flag at request_irq time, so it must be on CONFIG_CMDLINE, which is CMDLINE_FORCE here -- one line in CMDLINE_ADD, no code). Each arm is independently switchable, so this is four separate A/B arms, not one build.
evidence: artifacts/quake/placement-061521/run.log: /proc/interrupts deltas over a 15 s window mid-timedemo give riscv-timer 3400 (227/s) on CPU0 and 2958 (197/s) on CPU1, i2c 658 (44/s), esp32s31-lcd 776 (52/s), dw-mci 743 (50/s), pixel-accelerator 283 (19/s), dma ch24 344 (23/s), ch26 62 (4/s), wireless 39 (2.6/s) -- every device line is zero on CPU1

magnitude_estimate: 136 of 371 interrupts/s on CPU0 removed = 23 ms/s = 2.3% of CPU0; noirqdebug removes ~19 us from every remaining entry on both CPUs = a further ~0.6% of CPU0. Total ~2.5-3% of CPU0, which at Quake's 86%-busy main thread is roughly +2.5-3% fps (17.1 -> ~17.6). Zero RAM cost, no feature removed.
rule_check: Platform-only: two of our own drivers and one kernel command-line word. No app binary, config, wrapper or library touched. No feature disabled -- hw_vblank stays a runtime knob (the enable follows the param), the PPA fallback path stays, UNDERRUN stays enabled. Apps stay on SD. No RAM spent, so the 15.4 MB constraint is unaffected. Nothing upstream and mature is patched.
prior_attempts: The round-3 list contains 'stop the display drivers interrupting cpu0', which may overlap arms (1) and (2) -- I could not read the full text, so treat those two arms as possibly duplicate and the PPA/2D-DMA arm and the noirqdebug arm as new. The dead-end register has 'Touch-poll and hw_vblank as wakeup/CPU levers': hw_vblank=1 was measured as no change either way (119-136/s), which is a measurement of turning the hardware vblank ON, not of turning the no-op interrupt OFF -- the opposite direction, and it is consistent with this proposal (the interrupt is there whether or not anyone uses it). The dead-end 'PPA completion waiting' entry records the move TO spinning on the 2D-DMA EOF and to spinning rather than sleeping; nobody then removed the now-redundant interrupt. note_interrupt/noirqdebug appears nowhere in the register, the memory notes or docs/.

title: Take the display timebase from the scanout DMA's descriptor pointer, not from a free-running hrtimer
layer: kernel: drivers/gpu/drm/espressif/esp32s31-lcd.c + drivers/dma/esp32s31-axi-gdma.c
mechanism: Scanout is a free-running cyclic GDMA over the framebuffer, so the driver has no hardware vblank and fakes one with an hrtimer at the mode's frame period (esp32s31-lcd.c:365, started unconditionally at :1783). The driver's own comment at :133 admits the timer 'free-runs against scanout and drifts'. But the position is directly readable: the AXI GDMA exposes the current descriptor address (ESP32S31_AXI_TX_DSCR at 0x34, esp32s31-axi-gdma.c:60) and the driver already computes a per-period position from the descriptor list in esp32s31_axi_active_residue() (:1037) and the cyclic-residue path (:739-742). Reading that register gives the exact scan line with zero interrupts and zero drift. Three consequences: (a) the 42/s vblank hrtimer disappears entirely, along with its timer interrupt and its hrtimer_forward_now overrun bookkeeping; (b) drm_crtc_handle_vblank can be driven lazily -- only when something actually calls for a vblank count or timestamp -- so vblank becomes a polled query, not an event; (c) it makes beam-ordered presents possible for the first time: today the choice is wait_vblank=Y (49.2 ms/frame) or wait_vblank=N (42.6 ms, tearing), because the driver cannot tell where the beam is. With a real position the damage copy can be ordered behind the beam and be both tear-free and wait-free. This is the sweep's 'driven directly by DMA completion' case, applied to the one periodic event on this board that currently has no hardware source at all.
evidence: linux-71-port/drivers/gpu/drm/espressif/esp32s31-lcd.c:350-365 ('Scanout is free-running with no vblank interrupt, so vblank is emulated from a timer'), :133-134 ('a timer free-runs against scanout and drifts'), :1771-1784 (started unconditionally with the pipe), :2391-2404 (esp32s31_lcd_vblank_tick, with dbg_vblank_overruns counting periods it silently skipped), :4046-4087 (wait_vblank=Y 49.2/49.9/49.7 ms vs N 42.6/42.4/41.0 ms)
linux-71-port/drivers/dma/esp32s31-axi-gdma.c:60 ESP32S31_AXI_TX_DSCR, :739-742 cyclic current_period/residue computation, :1037 esp32s31_axi_active_residue

artifacts/quake/h1s-062518/syms.txt: esp32s31_lcd_vblank_tick 13 samples, drm_handle_vblank 9, drm_crtc_handle_vblank 5, plus the shared hrtimer machinery (hrtimer_interrupt 23, __hrtimer_run_queues 25, tick_program_event 25, clockevents_program_event 23)
artifacts/quake/placement-061521/run.log: CPU0 takes 227 timer interrupts/s against HZ=100, so ~127/s are hrtimers and the vblank tick at the panel's 42.1 Hz is the largest single named one
lvdesk never uses DRM vblank (no WAIT_VBLANK/PAGE_FLIP in lvdesk/kms.c or lvdesk/lvdesk.c), so today's hrtimer has no consumer while prompt_flip is on
magnitude_estimate: Removes ~42 timer interrupts/s from CPU0 at ~170 us of cold-flash entry = ~7 ms/s = 0.7% of CPU0 on its own. The beam-ordered present it enables is unquantified; the comparable past change (late present) was +13% on Doom, and the wait_vblank Y/N gap is 6.6 ms/frame, so there is room, but I would not claim it before measuring.
rule_check: Our own DRM and DMA drivers only. No app touched, no feature disabled (hw_vblank and prompt_flip stay as knobs), no RAM cost, no upstream code patched. Apps stay on SD.
prior_attempts: 'Retarget the cyclic scanout DMA at lvdesk's buffer' is in the dead-end register but is about what the DMA reads, not about reading where it is. 'Touch-poll and hw_vblank as wakeup/CPU levers' measured hw_vblank=1 (the LCD interrupt as the vblank source) as no change -- that arm swapped one interrupt for another; this one removes both. The round-3 list has 'scan out does the vertical scaling' and 'the panel is 60 hz not', which are about resolution and rate, not about phase. I found no prior reference anywhere to reading TX_DSCR as a scanout position.

title: Stop lvdesk's 62 Hz heartbeat while a fullscreen client owns the panel
layer: lvdesk/lvdesk.c main loop (our compositor)
mechanism: When a client is fullscreen, lvdesk switches the CRTC to the client's own mode buffer (kms_fs_enter) and presents from the draw callback (xwin_on_draw -> fs_present), so LVGL's widget tree is not on screen and its refresh timer has nothing to invalidate. Yet the loop still gates on FRAME_MS=16 and clamps the poll timeout to <=30 ms, so it wakes at least ~62 times a second: each wake is one armed hrtimer, one timer interrupt on CPU1 at the same ~170 us cold-flash entry price, two clock_gettime calls, an lv_timer_handler pass and a cursor_vis_update walk -- all on the hart that shares the single MSPI flash controller and the single D-cache with the game on CPU0. That servicing is not needed: xlite's ring doorbell is provably reliable (xlite.c:362 rings unless a bell is already pending, and xshim.c:9351-9373 drains the eventfd BEFORE clearing sig precisely so a wake can never be lost), and both the doorbell and the socket are in lvdesk's poll set, so the client's request wakes the loop immediately with no timeout. The fix is to pause LVGL's refresh timer while fs_active and let poll block on descriptors (with a long cap for the 5 s clock), rather than to set a shorter or fixed timeout.
evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:8878 #define FRAME_MS 16, :10176 frame_due gate, :10228 next = FRAME_MS - since, :10230 clamp to 30 ms, :10330 poll(fds, n, ms)
lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5871-5945 xwin_on_draw: when fs_active and id == fs_win it calls fs_present(id) and returns -- the fullscreen present is driven by the client's request, not by the LVGL frame tick
xlite/xlite.c:362-372 xlite_ring_bell (sig-guarded, one eventfd write per flush) and lvdesk/xshim.c:9351-9373 (read-then-clear ordering, with the 2026-09-20 lost-wake bug named and fixed)

artifacts/quake/placement-061521/run.log: CPU1 takes 197 timer interrupts/s against a 100 Hz tick, i.e. ~97/s of hrtimers on a core that owns no device and is 64% idle -- lvdesk's per-pass poll timeout is the obvious source
docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:890: CPU1's polling idle spun 460k traps/s on the shared flash/PSRAM bus and cost the canary +11%, establishing that CPU1 bus traffic is charged to CPU0
magnitude_estimate: Removes ~45-60 wakes/s from CPU1, each costing a timer interrupt (~170 us) plus an LVGL pass and ~8 syscalls: order 1-3% of a core on CPU1, of which an unknown but non-zero fraction is charged to CPU0 through the shared flash bus and D-cache. I would size it at +1-2% on the fullscreen timedemo and would not promise more.
rule_check: Our compositor only. The client is untouched and unaware. No feature disabled: input, the ctl fifo, the clock and the windowed path all keep their current behaviour; only the fullscreen case changes, and only the timeout. No RAM cost. Apps stay on SD.
prior_attempts: This was tried once and rejected, and the rejection is confounded. lvdesk.c:10199-10214 records: 'Skipping this while fullscreen and setting a fixed poll timeout instead collapsed the loop from ~500 passes per 5 s to 80, and prboom's OWN cpu fell from 1149 to 705 ticks over an identical 20 s window - the game using LESS cpu after freeing some up means it was rendering fewer frames.' Two problems with that: the arm skipped lv_timer_handler AND set a fixed timeout (so deferred output in xshim_flush(), which runs once per pass just before poll, was also delayed), and the verdict was taken on the client's CPU ticks rather than on fps, which was never reported for that arm. The proposal here does the opposite -- keep lv_timer_handler on its own schedule, pause only the refresh timer, keep xshim_flush per pass, and let the doorbell be the wake -- and must be judged on fps and on the frame-gap histogram, not on ticks. The round-3 list contains 'cut the compositor s frame at', which I take to be capping the compositor's rate at the panel rate; this is the different claim that in fullscreen the compositor has no frame at all.

title: CPU1 takes as many timer interrupts as CPU0 while owning no device: retest NO_HZ_IDLE now that the two bugs that plausibly killed it are fixed
layer: kernel config (Makefile TICK_TWEAKS) plus the lent-CPU interrupt path in drivers/irqchip/irq-esp32s31-clic.c
mechanism: The periodic tick is forced on (TICK_TWEAKS = --disable NO_HZ_IDLE --disable NO_HZ_COMMON --enable HZ_PERIODIC, Makefile:530), so every online CPU takes 100 ticks/s regardless of whether it has anything to do. Measured, CPU1 takes 197 timer interrupts/s while being 64% idle and taking zero device interrupts. On the lent hart every one of those is an emulated interrupt delivered through FreeRTOS, and it runs the same cold XIP timer path over the same single MSPI flash controller that CPU0 is fetching the game's kernel work from -- the mechanism by which CPU1 activity is charged to CPU0 is already established at +11% on the canary from the trapped-wfi polling idle. NO_HZ_IDLE was tried and abandoned in the dead-end register for 'lost a timer wake: silent hang, ~1 death per 2 runs'. That failure predates both of the fixes that address exactly that class of bug: patches/0057 (the CLIC level is never left, named as the root cause of every random SMP stall), and the hrtimer_rearm_deferred() flush now in esp32s31_clic_handle_irq (:919-932), whose comment says in so many words that without it 'the comparator stays stopped and queued timers (including DRM vblank and nanosleep) never fire until some unrelated wakeup' -- a lost timer wake on the lent CPU. The dead-end is therefore stale in its cause, not just in its date, and it is a config-only arm.
evidence: artifacts/quake/placement-061521/run.log: riscv-timer CPU1 delta 2958 over 15 s = 197/s, with every device IRQ line reading 0 for CPU1; CPU1 /proc/stat over the same window is user 19%, sys 17%, idle 64%
Makefile:530 TICK_TWEAKS forces HZ_PERIODIC; docs/current-state.md:7501-7519 records the NO_HZ_IDLE hang (~1 death per 2 runs vs 7/8 + 5/5 periodic) and that it broke /proc/stat
linux-71-port/drivers/irqchip/irq-esp32s31-clic.c:919-932: the deferred-hrtimer-rearm flush added for the lent CPU, with the comment describing precisely a lost timer wake
docs/smp-finish-plan.md 'Progress log': patches/0057 CLIC level drop, 'root cause of every SMP stall fixed', soak 5/5 -- both changes postdate the NO_HZ_IDLE attempt
docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:890: CPU1's 460k traps/s on the shared flash/PSRAM bus cost the canary +11%, so CPU1 interrupt traffic has a measured price on CPU0
magnitude_estimate: Removes up to 100 tick interrupts/s from CPU1 and lets its idle actually idle. Direct saving on CPU1 is ~1.7% of that core (100 x 170 us); the part that matters is the share charged to CPU0 through the shared MSPI, which is unmeasured but has a +11% precedent for a much larger trap rate. Honest range: +0.5-2% on the Quake timedemo, with a real chance of zero.
rule_check: Config only, plus no new code. Nothing app-side. No feature disabled. No RAM cost. The known risk is the old hang, so the arm must be gated on the existing soak (5+ boots to desktop and a full timedemo) before any performance number is believed, and /proc/stat correctness must be rechecked because NO_HZ_IDLE broke it last time.
prior_attempts: Directly contradicts a dead-end register entry ('Tickless idle (NO_HZ_IDLE)'), which is why the argument above is about the cause rather than the result: the recorded failure mode is a lost timer wake on the lent CPU, and two fixes for that exact failure mode have landed since. If it hangs again the entry should be re-closed with the new kernel number recorded, which is cheap. The round-3 list has 'hand the global tick duty tick', which I read as moving timekeeping duty to one CPU; that is a different mechanism (jiffies ownership) from stopping the idle CPU's tick, but if the existing candidate already proposes NO_HZ this one is redundant and should be dropped.
